question: across the whole corpus, does real V-JEPA 2 pooled geometry ever beat a frozen-random projection OF ITSELF (the projection-invariance test)
headline: Of every genuine frozen-random-substrate comparison in the corpus, real V-JEPA pooled geometry beats a random projection of itself in exactly ONE experiment (e7_sparse, and only in continual-forgetting dynamics by +0.075 to +0.124), and ties (adds nothing) in every other case including all decodability, geometry, and abstraction probes. The pooled substrate is projection-invariant almost everywhere; the only sliver of substrate-specific signal is in sparse-head forgetting, which is also the corpus one architectural positive.
